name: Philodemus of Gadara
bio: Philodemus of Gadara (c. 110 – c. 35 BC) was an Epicurean philosopher and a clever, light-hearted writer of epigrams. He lived in Italy under the patronage of Lucius Calpurnius Piso, and his library was found at Herculaneum.
The epigrams here are those that Paton's first volume ascribes to him by name.

poems.title: Book V, 4
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Philaenis, make drunk with oil the lamp, the silent confidant of things we may not speak of, and then go out: for Love alone loves no living witness ; and, Philaenis, shut the door close. And then, dear Xantho,—but thou, my bed, the lovers’ friend, learn now the rest of Aphrodite’s secrets.

poems.title: Book V, 13
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Charito has completed sixty years, but still the mass of her dark hair is as it was, and still upheld by no encircling band those marble cones of her bosom stand firm. Still her skin without a wrinkle distils ambrosia, distils fascination and ten thousand graces. Ye lovers who shrink not from fierce desire, come hither, unmindful of her decades.

poems.title: Book V, 24
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: My soul warns me to fly from the love of Heliodora, for well it knows the tears and jealousies of the past. It commands, but I have no strength to fly, for the shameless girl herself warns me to leave her, and even while she warns she kisses me.

poems.title: Book V, 25
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: As often as I come to Cydilla’s embrace, whether I ' come in the day time, or more venturesome still in the evening, I know that I hold my path on the edge of a precipice, I know that each time I recklessly stake my life. But what advantage is it to me to know that? My heart is bold (?), and when Love ever leads it, it knows not at all even the shadow of fear.

poems.title: Book V, 46
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: He. Good-evening. She. Good-evening. He. What may your name be? Ske. And yours? He. Don’t be so inquisitive all at once. She. Well don’t you. He. Are you engaged? Ske. To anyone that likes me. He. Will you come to supper to-night? She. If you like. He. Very well! How much shall it be? She. Don’t give me anything in advance. He. That is strange. She. Give me what you think right after sleeping with me. He. That is quite fair. Where do you live? I willsend. She. I will tell you. He. And when will youcome? She. Any time you like. He. I would like now. She. Then go on in front.

poems.title: Book V, 107
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: “I know, charming lady, how to love him who loves me, and again I know right well how to bite him who bites me. Do not vex too much one who loves thee, or try to provoke the heavy wrath of the Muses.” So I ever cried to thee and warned, but thou didst hearken to my words no more than the Ionian Sea. So now thou sobbest sorely and complainest, while I sit in Naias’ lap.

poems.title: Book V, 112
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: I loved. Who hath not? I made revels in her honour. Who is uninitiated in those mysteries? But I was distraught. By whom? Was it not by a god ?—Good-bye to it; for already the grey locks hurry on to replace the black, and tell me I have reached the age of discretion. While it was playtime I played ; now it is over I will turn to more worthy thoughts.

poems.title: Book V, 115
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: I fell in love with Demo of Paphos—nothing surprising in that: and again with Demo of Samos— well that was not so remarkable: and thirdly with Demo of Naxos—then the matter ceased to be a joke : and in the fourth place with Demo of Argos. The Fates themselves seem to have christened me Philodeme?; as I always feel ardent desire for some Demo.

poems.title: Book V, 120
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: By midnight, eluding my husband, and drenched by the heavy rain, I came. And do we then sit idle, not talking and sleeping, as lovers ought to sleep?

poems.title: Book V, 121
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Philaenion is short and rather too dark, but her hair is more curled than parsley, and her skin is more tender than down: there is more magic in her voice than in the cestus of Venus, and she never refuses me anything and often refrains from begging for a present. Such a Philaenion grant me, golden Cypris, to love, until I find another more perfect.

poems.title: Book V, 123
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Sune, Moon of the night, horned Moon, who lovest to look on revels, shine through the lattice and let thy light fall on golden Callistion. It is no offence for an immortal to pry into the secrets of lovers. Thou dost bless her and me, I know,O Moon ; for did not Endymion set thy soul afire

poems.title: Book V, 124
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Thy summer's flower hath not yet burst from the bud, the grape that puts forth its first virgin charm is yet green, but already the young Loves sharpen their swift arrows, Lysidice, and a hidden fire is smouldering. Let us fly, we unlucky lovers, before the arrow is on the string. I foretell right soon a vast conflagration.

poems.title: Book V, 126
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: So-and-so gives so-and-so five talents for once, and possesses her in fear and trembling, and, by Heaven, she is not even pretty. I give Lysianassa five drachmas for twelve times, and she is better looking, and there is no secret about it. Either I have lost my wits, or he ought to be rendered incapable of such conduct for the fature.

poems.title: Book V, 131
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Xanthippe’s touch on the lyre, and her talk, and her speaking eyes, and her singing, and the fire that is just alight, will burn thee, my heart, but from what beginning or when or how I know not. Thou, unhappy heart, shalt know when thou art smouldering.

poems.title: Book V, 132
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: O feet, O legs, O thighs for which I justly died, O nates, O pectinem, O flanks, O shoulders, O breasts, O slender neck, O arms, O eyes I am mad for, O accomplished movement, O admirable kisses, O exclamations that excite! If she is Italian and her name is Flora and she does not sing Sappho, yet Perseus was in love with Indian Andromeda.

poems.title: Book V, 306: Addressed by a Girl to a Man
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: You weep, you speak in piteous accents, you look strangely at me, you are jealous, you touch me often and go on kissing me. That is like a lover; but when I say “Here I am next you” and you dawdle, you have absolutely nothing of the lover in you.

poems.title: Book VI, 349
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: O Meticertes, son of Ino, and thou sea-blue queen of the sea, Leucothea, goddess that avertest evil, and ye Nereids linked in the dance, and ye waves, and thou, Poseidon, and Thracian Zephyr, gentlest of winds, be gracious unto me and bear me, escaping the broad billows, safe to the sweet beach of Piraeus.

poems.title: Book VII, 222
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Here lies the tender body of the tender being; here lies Trygonion the ornament of the wanton band of the emasculated, he who was at home by the holy shrine of Rhea, amid the noise of music and the gay prattling throng, the darling of the Mother of the gods, he who alone among his effeminate fellows really loved the rites of Cypris, and whose charms came near those of Lais. Give birth, thou holy soil, round the grave-stone of the maenad not to brambles but to the soft petals of white violets,

poems.title: Book IX, 412
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: It is already the season of the rose, Sosylus, and of ripe chick-peas, and the first cut cabbages, and smelts, and fresh salted cheese, and the tender leaves of curly lettuces. But we do not go up to the pleasaunce or sit on the belvedere, Sosylus, as we used. Yet Antigenes and Bacchius were sporting but yesterday, and to-day we carry them to their graves.

poems.title: Book IX, 570
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Xantho, modelled of wax, with scented skin, with a face like a Muse’s, sweet-voiced, fair darling of the twin-winged Loves, play to me with thy scent-bedewed hands. “I must lie and sleep for long, dying not, on a single bed cut out of stone.” Sing it to me again, Xantho dear; yea! yea! sing me that sweet song. [Dost thou not hear it, man who amassest interest of moneys? On a single bed cut out of stone thou shalt live for ever, unhappy wretch.]

poems.title: Book X, 21
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Cypris of the Calm, lover of bridegrooms ; Cypris, ally of the just; Cypris, mother of the tempest-footed Loves; save me, Cypris, a man but half torn away from my saffron bridal chamber, and chilled now to the soul by the snows of Gaul. Save me, Cypris, thy peaceful servant, who utters no vain words to any, tossed as I am now on thy deep blue sea! Cypris, who lovest to bring ships to port, who lovest the solemn rites of wedlock, save me now, my queen, and bring me to the haven of my Naias.

poems.title: Book X, 103
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Neither look into nor pass by (the place where they sell scarce delicacies ?). Now be off to the tripe-stall to spend a drachma. One fig too at times may cost a drachma, but if you wait, it will buy you a thousand. Time is the poor man’s god.

poems.title: Book XI, 34
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: I wish no garlands of white violets again, no lyre-playing again, no Chian wine again, no Syrian myrrh again, no revelling again, no thirsty whore with me again. I hate these things that lead to madness. But bind my head with narcissus and let me taste the crooked flute, and anoint my limbs with saffron ointment, wet my gullet with wine of Mytilene and mate me with a virgin who will love her nest.

poems.title: Book XI, 35
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Artemidorus gave us a cabbage, Aristarchus caviare, Athenagoras little onions, Philodemus a small liver, and Apollophanes two pounds of pork, and there were three pounds still over from yesterday. Go and buy us an egg and garlands and sandals and scent, and I wish them to be here at four o’clock sharp.

poems.title: Book XI, 41
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Seven years added to thirty are gone already like so many pages torn out of my life ; already, Xanthippe, my head is sprinkled with grey hairs, messengers of the age of wisdom. But still I care for the speaking music of the lyre and for revelling, and in my insatiate heart the fire is alive. But ye Muses, my mistresses, bring it to a close at once with the words “ Xanthippe is the end of my madness.”’

poems.title: Book XI, 44
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: To-morrow, dearest Piso, your friend, beloved by the Muses, who keeps our annual feast of the twentieth invites you to come after the ninth hour to his simple cottage. If you miss udders and draughts of Chian wine, you will see at least sincere friends and you will hear things far sweeter than the land of the Phaeacians. But if you ever cast your eyes on me, Piso, we shall celebrate the twentieth richly instead of simply.

poems.title: Book XI, 318
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Anticrates knew the constellations much better than Aratus, but could not tell his own nativity ; for he said he was in doubt whether he was born in the Ram or the Twins, or in both the Fishes. But it was clearly found to be in all three, for he is a tupper and a fool, and effeminate, and fond of fish.

poems.title: Book XII, 173
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: Demo and Thermion are killing me. Thermion is a courtesan and Demo a girl who knows not Cypris yet. The one I touch, but the other I may not. By thyself, Cypris, I swear, I know not which I should call the more desirable. I will say it is the virgin Demo; for I desire not what is ready to hand, but long for whatever is kept under lock and key.

poems.title: Book XVI, 234
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text: The stone has place for three immortals; for the head clearly shows me to be goat-horned Pan, the breast and belly tell I am Heracles, the rest of the thighs and the legs are the portion of wing-footed Hermes. Refuse me not a sacrifice, stranger, for thy one sacrifice will earn the thanks of the three gods.

poems.title: Love and Reason (Mackail)
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: My soul forewarns me to flee the desire of Heliodora, knowing well the tears and jealousies of old. She talks; but I have no strength to flee, for, shameless that she is, she forewarns, and while she forewarns, she loves.

poems.title: Moonlight (Mackail)
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Lady of Night, twy-horned, lover of nightlong revels, shine, O Moon, shine, darting through the latticed windows; shed thy splendour on golden Callistion; thine immortality may look down unchidden on the deeds of lovers; thou dost bless both her and me, I know, O Moon; for thy soul too was fired by Endymion.

poems.title: To the Gods of Sea and Weather (Mackail)
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: O Melicerta son of Ino, and thou, sea-green Leucothea, mistress of Ocean, deity that shieldest from harm, and choirs of the Nereïds, and waves, and thou Poseidon, and Thracian Zephyrus, gentlest of the winds, carry me propitiously, sped through the broad wave, safe to the sweet shore of the Peiraeus.

poems.title: The Flower Unblown (Mackail)
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Not yet is thy summer unfolded from the bud, nor does the purple come upon thy grape that throws out the first shoots of its maiden graces; but already the young Loves are whetting their fleet arrows, Lysidice, and the hidden fire is smouldering. Flee we, wretched lovers, ere yet the shaft is on the string; I prophesy a mighty burning soon.

poems.title: Epilogue (Mackail)
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: I was in love once; who has not been? I have revelled; who is uninitiated in revels? nay, I was mad; at whose prompting but a god's? Let them go; for now the silver hair is fast replacing the black, a messenger of wisdom that comes with age. We too played when the time of playing was; and now that it is no longer, we will turn to worthier thoughts.

poems.title: Returning Spring (Mackail)
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Now is rose-time and peas are in season, and the heads of early cabbage, O Sosylus, and the milky maena, and fresh-curdled cheese, and the soft-springing leaves of curled lettuces; and do we neither pace the foreland nor climb to the outlook, as always, O Sosylus, we did before? for Antagoras and Bacchius too frolicked yesterday, and now to-day we bear them forth for burial.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.4: τὸν σιγῶντα, Φιλαινί, συνίστορα τῶν ἀλαλήτων
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
τὸν σιγῶντα, Φιλαινί, συνίστορα τῶν ἀλαλήτων
λύχνον ἐλαιηρῆς ἐκμεθύσασα δρόσου,
ἔξιθι· μαρτυρίην γὰρ Ἔρως μόνος οὐκ ἐφίλησεν
ἔμπνουν καὶ πηκτὴν κλεῖε, Φιλαινί, θύρην.
καὶ σύ, φίλη Ξανθώ, με· σὺ δʼ, ὦ φιλεράστρια κοίτη,
ἤδη τῆς Παφίης ἴσθι τὰ λειπόμενα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.13: ἑξήκοντα τελεῖ Χαριτὼ λυκαβαντίδας ὥρας,
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
ἑξήκοντα τελεῖ Χαριτὼ λυκαβαντίδας ὥρας,
ἀλλʼ ἔτι κυανέων σύρμα μένει πλοκάμων,
κἠν στέρνοις ἔτι κεῖνα τὰ λύγδινα κώνια μαστῶν
ἕστηκεν, μίτρης γυμνὰ περιδρομάδος,
καὶ χρὼς ἀρρυτίδωτος ἔτʼ ἀμβροσίην, ἔτι πειθὼ
πᾶσαν, ἔτι στάζει μυριάδας χαρίτων.
ἀλλὰ πόθους ὀργῶντας ὅσοι μὴ φεύγετʼ ἐρασταί,
δεῦρʼ ἴτε, τῆς ἐτέων ληθόμενοι δεκάδος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.25: ὁσσάκι Κυδίλλης ὑποκόλπιος, εἴτε κατʼ ἦμαρ,
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
ὁσσάκι Κυδίλλης ὑποκόλπιος, εἴτε κατʼ ἦμαρ,
εἴτʼ ἀποτολμήσας ἤλυθον ἑσπέριος,
οἶδʼ ὅτι πὰρ κρημνὸν τέμνω πόρον, οἶδʼ ὅτι ῥιπτῶ
πάντα κύβον κεφαλῆς αἰὲν ὕπερθεν ἐμῆς.
ἀλλὰ τί μοι πλέον ἐστί; †   γὰρ θρασύς, ἠδʼ ὅταν ἕλκῃ
πάντοτʼ Ἔρως, ἀρχὴν οὐδʼ ὄναρ οἶδε φόβου.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.46: α. χαιρε σύ. β. καὶ σύ
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.107: “ γινώσκω, χαρίεσσα, φιλεῖν πάνυ τὸν
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
“ γινώσκω, χαρίεσσα, φιλεῖν πάνυ τὸν φιλέοντα,
καὶ πάλι γινώσκω τόν με δακόντα δακεῖν
μὴ λύπει με λίην στέργοντά σε, μηδʼ ἐρεθίζειν
τὰς βαρυοργήτους σοι θέλε Πιερίδας.”
τοῦτʼ ἐβόων αἰεὶ καὶ προὔλεγον ἀλλʼ ἴσα πόντῳ
Ἰονίῳ μύθων ἔκλυες ι;ἡμετέρων.
τοιγὰρ νῦν σὺ μὲν ὧδε μέγα κλαίουσα βαΰζεις·
ἡμεῖς δʼ ἐν κόλποις ἥμεθα Ναϊάδος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.112: ἠράσθην τίς δʼ οὐχί; κεκώμακα· τίς
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
ἠράσθην τίς  δʼ οὐχί; κεκώμακα· τίς  δʼ ἀμύητος
κώμων; ἀλλʼ ἐμάνην ἐκ τίνος; οὐχὶ θεοῦ;
ἐρρίφθω· πολιὴ γὰρ ἐπείγεται ἀντὶ μελαίνης
θρὶξ ἤδη, συνετῆς ἄγγελος ἡλικίης.
καὶ παίζειν ὅτε καιρός, ἐπαίξαμεν ἡνίκα καὶ νῦν
οὐκέτι, λωϊτέρης φροντίδος ἁψόμεθα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.115: ἠράσθην Δημοῦς Παφίης γένος· οὐ μέγα
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
ἠράσθην Δημοῦς Παφίης γένος· οὐ μέγα θαῦμα
καὶ Σαμίης Δημοῦς δεύτερον οὐχὶ μέγα·
καὶ πάλι Ναξιακῆς Δημοῦς τρίτον οὐκέτι ταῦτα
παίγνια· καὶ Δημοῦς τέτρατον Ἀργολίδος.
αὐταί που Μοῖραί με κατωνόμασαν Φιλόδημον,
ὡς αἰεὶ Δημοῦς θερμὸς ἔχει με πόθος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.120: καὶ νυκτὸς μεσάτης τὸν ἐμὸν κλέψασα
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
καὶ νυκτὸς μεσάτης τὸν ἐμὸν κλέψασα σύνευνον
ἦλθον, καὶ πυκινῇ τεγγομένη ψακάδι.
τοὔνεκʼ ἐν ἀπρήκτοισι καθήμεθα, κοὐχὶ λαλεῦντες
εὕδομεν, ὡς εὕδειν τοῖς φιλέουσι θέμις;

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.121: Μικκὴ καὶ μελανεῦσα Φιλαίνιον, ἀλλὰ σελίνων
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
Μικκὴ καὶ μελανεῦσα Φιλαίνιον, ἀλλὰ σελίνων
οὐλοτέρη, καὶ μνοῦ χρῶτα τερεινοτέρη,
καὶ κεστοῦ φωνεῦσα μαγώτερα, καὶ παρέχουσα
πάντα, καὶ αἰτῆσαι πολλάκι φειδομένη·
τοιαύτην στέργοιμι Φιλαίνιον, ἄχρις ἂν εὕρω
ἄλλην, ὦ χρυσέη Κύπρι, τελειοτέρην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.123: Νυκτερινή, δίκερως, φιλοπάννυχε, φαῖνε, Σελήνη,
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
Νυκτερινή, δίκερως, φιλοπάννυχε, φαῖνε, Σελήνη,
φαῖνε, διʼ εὐτρήτων βαλλομένη θυρίδων
αὔγαζε χρυσέην Καλλίστιον ἐς τὰ φιλεύντων
ἔργα κατοπτεύειν οὐ φθόνος ἀθανάτῃ.
ὀλβίζεις καὶ τήνδε καὶ ἡμέας, οἶδα, Σελήνη·
καὶ γὰρ σὴν ψυχὴν ἔφλεγεν Ἐνδυμίων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.124: οὔπω σοι καλύκων γυμνὸν θέρος, οὐδὲ
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
οὔπω σοι καλύκων γυμνὸν θέρος, οὐδὲ μελαίνει
βότρυς ὁ παρθενίους πρωτοβολῶν χάριτας·
ἀλλʼ ἤδη θοὰ τόξα νέοι θήγουσιν Ἔρωτες,
Λυσιδίκη, καὶ πῦρ τύφεται ἐγκρύφιον.
φεύγωμεν, δυσέρωτες, ἕως βέλος οὐκ ἐπὶ νευρῇ·
μάντις ἐγὼ μεγάλης αὐτίκα πυρκαϊῆς.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.126: πέντε δίδωσιν ἑνὸς τῇ δεῖνα ὁ
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
πέντε δίδωσιν ἑνὸς τῇ δεῖνα ὁ δεῖνα τάλαντα,
καὶ βινεῖ φρίσσων, καὶ μὰ τὸν οὐδὲ καλὴν
πέντε δʼ ἐγὼ δραχμὰς τῶν δώδεκα Λυσιανάσσῃ,
καὶ βινῶ πρὸς τῷ κρείσσονα καὶ φανερῶς.
πάντως ἤτοι ἐγὼ φρένας οὐκ ἔχω, ἢ τό γε λοιπὸν
τοὺς κείνου πελέκει δεῖ διδύμους ἀφελεῖν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.131: ψαλμός, καὶ λαλιή, καὶ κωτίλον ὄμμα,
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
ψαλμός, καὶ λαλιή, καὶ κωτίλον ὄμμα, καὶ ᾠδὴ
Ξανθίππης, καὶ πῦρ ἄρτι καταρχόμενον,
ὦ ψυχή, φλέξει σε· τὸ δʼ ἐκ τίνος, ἢ πότε, καὶ πῶς,
οὐκ οἶδα· γνώσῃ, δύσμορε, τυφομένη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.132: ὦ ποδός, ὦ κνήμης, ὦ τῶν
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
ὦ ποδός, ὦ κνήμης, ὦ τῶν ἀπόλωλα δικαίως
μηρῶν, ὦ γλουτῶν, ὦ κτενός, ὦ λαγόνων,
ὦ ὤμοιν, ὦ μαστῶν, ὦ τοῦ ῥαδινοῖο τραχήλου,
ὦ χειρῶν, ὦ τῶν μαίνομαι ὀμματίων,
ὦ κατατεχνοτάτου κινήματος, ὦ περιάλλων
γλωττισμῶν, ὦ τῶν θῦʼ ἐμὲ φωναρίων.
εἰ δʼ Ὀπικὴ καὶ Φλῶρα καὶ οὐκ ᾄδουσα τὰ Σαπφοῦς,
καὶ Περσεὺς Ἰνδῆς ἠράσατʼ Ἀνδρομέδης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.306: δακρύεις, ἐλεεινὰ λαλεῖς, περίεργα θεωρεῖς,
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
δακρύεις, ἐλεεινὰ λαλεῖς, περίεργα θεωρεῖς,
ζηλοτυπεῖς, ἅπτῃ πολλάκι,πυκνὰ φιλεῖς.
ταῦτα μέν ἐστιν ἐρῶντος· ὅταν δʼ εἴπω παράκειμαι ,
καὶ μέλλῃς, ἁπλῶς οὐδὲν ἐρῶντος ἔχεις.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.349: Ἰνοῦς ὦ Μελικέρτα, σύ τε γλαυκὴ
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
Ἰνοῦς ὦ Μελικέρτα, σύ τε γλαυκὴ μεδέουσα
Λευκοθέη πόντου, δαῖμον ἀλεξίκακε,
Νηρῄδων τε χοροί, καὶ κύματα, καὶ σύ, Πόσειδον,
καὶ Θρήιξ, ἀνέμων πρηΰτατε, Ζέφυρε,
ἵλαοί με φέροιτε, διὰ πλατὺ κῦμα φυγόντα,
σῶον ἐπὶ γλυκερὰν ᾐόνα Πειραέως.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.222: ἐνθάδε τῆς τρυφερῆς μαλακὸν ῥέθος, ἐνθάδε
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
ἐνθάδε τῆς τρυφερῆς μαλακὸν ῥέθος, ἐνθάδε κεῖται
Τρυγόνιον, σαβακῶν ἄνθεμα Σαλμακίδων
ᾗ καλύβη καὶ δοῦπος ἐνέπρεπεν, ᾗ φιλοπαίγμων
στωμυλίη, Μήτηρ ἣν ἐφίλησε θεῶν
ἡ μούνη στέρξασα τὰ Κύπριδος ἡμιγυναίκων
ὄργια, καὶ φίλτρων Λαΐδος ἁψαμένη.
φῦε κατὰ στήλης, ἱερὴ κόνι, τῇ φιλοβάκχῳ
μὴ βάτον, ἀλλʼ ἁπαλὰς λευκοΐων κάλυκας.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.412: ἤδη καὶ ῥόδον ἐστί, καὶ ἀκμάζων
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
ἤδη καὶ ῥόδον ἐστί, καὶ ἀκμάζων ἐρέβινθος,
καὶ καυλοὶ κράμβης, Σωσύλε, πρωτοτόμου,
καὶ μαίνη ʽʼσαλαγεῦσα, καὶ ἀρτιπαγὴς ἁλίτυρος,
καὶ θριδάκων οὔλων ἁβροφυῆ πέταλα.
ἡμεῖς δʼ οὔτʼ ἀκτῆς ἐπιβαίνομεν, οὔτʼ ἐν ἀπόψει
γινόμεθʼ, ὡς αἰεί, Σωσύλε, τὸ πρότερον;
καὶ μὴν Ἀντιγένης καὶ Βάκχιος ἐχθὲς ἔπαιζον·
νῦν δʼ αὐτοὺς θάψαι σήμερον ἐκφέρομεν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.570: Ξανθώ, κηρόπλαστε, μυρόχροε, μουσοπρόσωπε,
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
Ξανθώ, κηρόπλαστε, μυρόχροε, μουσοπρόσωπε,
εὔλαλε, διπτερύγων καλὸν ἄγαλμα Πόθων,
ψῆλόν μοι χερσὶ δροσιναῖς μύρον· “ἐν μονοκλίνῳ
δεῖ με λιθοδμήτῳ δή ποτε πετριδίῳ
εὕδειν ἀθανάτως πουλὺν χρόνον”  ᾆδε πάλιν μοι,
Ξανθάριον, ναί, ναί, τὸ γλυκὺ τοῦτο μέλος.
[οὐκ ἀίεις, ὤνθρωφʼ, ὁ τοκογλύφος; ἐν μονοκλίνῳ
δεῖ σὲ βιοῦν αἰεί, δύσμορε, πετριδίῳ.] ˘

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.21: Κύπρι γαληναίη, φιλονύμφιε, Κύπρι δικαίων
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
Κύπρι γαληναίη, φιλονύμφιε, Κύπρι δικαίων
σύμμαχε, Κύπρι Πόθων μῆτερ ἀελλοπόδων,
Κύπρι, τὸν ἡμίσπαστον ἀπὸ κροκέων ἐμὲ παστῶν,
τὸν χιόσι ψυχὴν Κελτίσι νιφόμενον,
Κύπρι, τὸν ἡσύχιόν με, τὸν οὐδενὶ κοῦφα λαλεῦντα,
τὸν σέο πορφυρέῳ κλυζόμενον πελάγει,
Κύπρι φιλορμίστειρα, φιλόργιε, σῷζέ με, Κύπρι,
Ναϊακοὺς ἤδη, δεσπότι, πρὸς λιμένας.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.103: τὴν † προτερον θυμέλην μήτʼ ἔμβλεπε,
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
τὴν †   προτερον θυμέλην μήτʼ ἔμβλεπε, μήτε παρέλθῃς·
νῦν ἄπαγε δραχμῆς εἰς κολοκορδόκολα.
καὶ σῦκον δραχμῆς ἓν γίνεται· ἢν δʼ ἀναμείνῃς,
χίλια. τοῖς πτωχοῖς ὁ χρόνος ἐστὶ θεός.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.34: Λευκοΐνους πάλι δὴ καὶ ψάλματα, καὶ
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
Λευκοΐνους πάλι δὴ καὶ ψάλματα, καὶ πάλι Χίους
οἴνους, καὶ πάλι δὴ σμύρναν ἔχειν Συρίην,
καὶ πάλι κωμάζειν, καὶ ἔχειν πάλι διψάδα πόρνην
οὐκ ἐθέλω· μισῶ ταὺτα τὰ πρὸς μανίην.
ἀλλά με ναρκίσσοις ἀναδήσατε, καὶ πλαγιαύλων
γεύσατε, καὶ κροκίνοις χρίσατε γυῖα μύροις,
καὶ Μυτιληναίῳ τὸν πνεύμονα τέγξατε Βάκχῳ,
καὶ συζεύξατέ μοι φωλάδα παρθενικήν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.35: Κράμβην Ἀρτεμίδωρος, Ἀρίσταρχος δὲ τάριχον,
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
Κράμβην Ἀρτεμίδωρος, Ἀρίσταρχος δὲ τάριχον,
βολβίσκους δʼ ἡμῖν δῶκεν Ἀθηναγόρας,
ἡπάτιον Φιλόδημος, Ἀπολλοφάνης δὲ δύο μνᾶς
χοιρείου, καὶ τρεῖς ἦσαν ἀπʼ ἐχθὲς ἔτι.
ᾠόν, καὶ στεφάνους, καὶ σάμβαλα, καὶ μύρον ἡμῖν
λάμβανε, καὶ δεκάτης εὐθὺ θέλω παράγειν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.41: ἑπτὰ τριηκόντεσσιν ἐπέρχονται λυκάβαντες,
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
ἑπτὰ τριηκόντεσσιν ἐπέρχονται λυκάβαντες,
ἤδη μοι βιότου σχιζόμεναι σελίδες·
ἤδη καὶ λευκαί με κατασπείρουσιν ἔθειραι,
Ξανθίππη, συνετῆς ἄγγελοι ἡλικίης.
ἀλλʼ ἔτι μοι ψαλμός τε λάλος κῶμοί τε μέλονται,
καὶ πῦρ ἀπλήστῳ τύφετʼ ἐνὶ κραδίῃ.
αὐτὴν ἀλλὰ τάχιστα κορωνίδα γράψατε, Μοῦσαι,
ταύτην ἡμετέρης, δεσπότιδες, μανίης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.44: αὔριον εἰς λιτήν σε καλιάδα, φίλτατε
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
αὔριον εἰς λιτήν σε καλιάδα, φίλτατε Πείσων,
ἐξ ἐνάτης ἕλκει μουσοφιλὴς ἕταρος,
εἰκάδα δειπνίζων ἐνιαύσιον· εἰ δʼ ἀπολείψεις
οὔθατα καὶ Βρομίου χιογενῆ πρόποσιν,
ἀλλʼ ἑτάρους ὄψει παναληθέας, ἀλλʼ ἐπακούσῃ
Φαιήκων γαίης πουλὺ μελιχρότερα·
ἢν δέ ποτε στρέψῃς καὶ ἐς ἡμέας ὄμματα, Πείσων,
ἄξομεν ἐκ λιτῆς εἰκάδα πιοτέρην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.318: Ἀντικράτης ᾔδει τὰ σφαιρικὰ μᾶλλον Ἀράτου
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
Ἀντικράτης ᾔδει τὰ σφαιρικὰ μᾶλλον Ἀράτου
πολλῷ, τὴν ἰδίην δʼ οὐκ ἐνόει γένεσιν
διστάζειν γὰρ ἔφη, πότερʼ ἐν κριῷ γεγένηται
ἢ διδύμοις, ἢ τοῖς ἰχθύσιν ἀμφοτέροις.
εὕρηται δὲ σαφῶς ἐν τοῖς τρισί καὶ γὰρ ὀχευτὴς
καὶ μωρὸς μαλακὸς τʼ ἐστὶ καὶ ὀψοφάγος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XII.173: Δημώ με κτείνει καὶ Θέρμιον ἡ
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
Δημώ με κτείνει καὶ Θέρμιον ἡ μὲν ἑταίρη,
Δημονόη ˘ δʼ οὔπω Κύπριν ἐπισταμένη.
καὶ τῆς μὲν ψαύω· τῆς δʼ οὐ θέμις. οὐ μὰ σέ, Κύπρι,
οὐκ οἶδʼ ἣν εἰπεῖν δεῖ με ποθεινοτέρην.
Δημάριον λέξω τὴν παρθένον οὐ γὰρ ἕτοιμα
βούλομαι, ἀλλὰ ποθῶ πᾶν τὸ φυλασσόμενον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.234: Τρισσοὺς ἀθανάτους χωρεῖ λίθος· ἁ κεφαλὰ
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
Τρισσοὺς ἀθανάτους χωρεῖ λίθος· ἁ κεφαλὰ γὰρ
μανύει τρανῶς Πᾶνα τὸν αἰγόκερων,
στέρνα δὲ καὶ νηδὺς Ἡρακλέα, λοιπὰ δὲ μηρῶν
καὶ κνήμης Ἑρμῆς ὁ πτερόπους ἔλαχεν.
θύειν ἀρνήσῃ, ξένε, μηκέτι· τοῦ γὰρ ἑνός σοι
θύματος οἱ τρισσοὶ δαίμονες ἀντόμεθα,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.30: ὁ πρὶν ἐγὼ καὶ πέντε καὶ
poems.author: Philodemus of Gadara
poems.text:
ὁ πρὶν ἐγὼ καὶ πέντε καὶ ἐννέα, νῦν, Ἀφροδίτη,
ἓν μόλις ἐκ πρώτης νυκτὸς ἐς ἠέλιον
οἴμοι καὶ . . τοῦτο κατὰ βραχὺ ʽ πολλάκι δʼ ἤδη
ἡμιθανὲσʼ θνῄσκει· τοῦτο τὸ τερμέριον.
ὦ γῆρας, γῆρας, τί ποθʼ ὕστερον, ἢν ἀφίκηαι,
ποιήσεις, ὅτε νῦν ὧδε μαραίνομεθα;
